The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, December 1, 1933

Rowdies Here Attack
Office Of Society Said
Backing Fukien Rebels

Hammers Shatter Show Cases Of Shenchow
Kuokwang Publishing Concern Owned
By Revolting General

Clash Looms On Chekiang Border

The Shenchow Kuokwang Publishing Society, alleged Socialist
Democratic propaganda organ under General Chen Ming-shu,
independence leader in Fukien, was made a target of attack by
local rowdies, believed to be elements of Fascist organizations,
at 7 o'clock last night.
A youth, clad in long gown, entered the bookstore at 136
Honan Road, pretending to be a customer, according to the shop-
assistants today. When he reached the counter, he gave a signal,
promptly responded to by three rowdies. They started wrecking
the premises, shattering the show
cases with hammers and escaped
before the arrival of police officers.
Police Arrest Youth
A Chinese policeman, however,
accosted a youth clad in long gown
at corner of Honan and Siking
Roads. He was bleeding and it was
alleged that he was the man who
first entered the bookstore. It also
was said that his head was cut by
flying glass while hammering a
show case.
Taken to the station, the youth
emphatically denied the charge,
adding that he received in the in-
jury accidentally as a piece of glass
fell on his forehead. He was dis-
missed at the police station as no
incriminating evidence could be
found against him.
It is understood that no alarm
was raised by the shop-assistants
during or after the attack.

Attack on propaganda organ of Social Democratic
Party - book shop smashed

At 7 p.m. November 30, four Chinese entered the
Shun Chow Kuo Kwan; Zoe, a Book Shop at 136 Honan Road,
and after cutting the telephone wire smashed a show
window and cupboard. The miscreants subsequently
departed leaving behind paper slips bearing anti-Communist
and pro-Chiang Kai-shek slogans. A male Chinese who was
in the shop at the time was suspected of being one of the
trouble makers and was arrested by the police but subse-
quently released for lack of evidence against him.

This book shop is suspected of being a propaganda
organ of the Social Democratic Party of which General
Chen Ling-chu (陳銘樞) one of the principal promoters
of the Fukien Incident, is the leader.

With reference to attached reports dated November 20
and December 15 made by D.S. Pitts on the above subject,
diligent enquiries have been kept up by the staff of S.1
but nothing definite can be ascertained regarding the
so-called "上海電影界剋共團 Shanghai Cinema Circles Communist Extermination
Association" or the persons responsible for the attacks
on the bookstores.
While it is reasonable to believe that ex-graduates
of the Whampoa Military Academy who may be members of the
"Blue Shirts Society", engineered the attacks on the Nee
Hwa Motion Picture Studio and the Liang Yue Bookstore,
no proof of this has been forthcoming and it is more likely
that a few irresponsible students with ultra-patriotic ideas
were the guilty parties.
Such an Association as above mentioned, being
of an anti-Communist character would undoubtedly have at
least the moral support of local Government officials.
Nothing further has been heard of the Association since the
attack on the Shun Chow Kuo Kwang Dzoe (神州國光社) Bookstore,
136 Honan Road, on November 30 and it appears as if its
activities have come to an end.

At 7.30 p.m. 17-11-53, complainant came
to this Station with a piece of stone wrapped up
in a piece of white paper bearing Chinese charac-
ters, copy of translation is attached hereto, and
reported that at 7.15 p.m., same date, it had been
thrown through one of the plate glass windows of
a silver ware shop at 319 Nanking Road, by a
person unknown, who escaped unseen by the occu-
pants of the shop. D.S. Logan and C.D.C.105
visited the scene and found a large plate glass
window damaged to the extent of $100.00. The
shop in question is situated on the South side
of Nanking Road almost directly opposite the inter-
section of Lloyd Road, where C.P.C.2466 was posted
on point duty some 30 yards distant but the latter
though he heard the smashing of the window pane
did not see any person running from the scene and
was not able to single out any suspicious person
in the vicinity at the time due to the density of
the crowds walking on the pavement. Inquiries
made by C.P.C.2466 immediately after the occur-
rence failed to locate a witness of the offence
as also did enquiries made in the vicinity by
D.S. Logan and C.D.C.105.

The malicious damage would appear to be
the work of Communists inspired by the action of
complainant and various other shopkeepers exhibit-
ing in their shop windows, posters denouncing the
Communists and asking for support for the Nanking
Government.

In compliance with the instructions of the Officer i/c

elicit the following information:-

The Hsin Kwang Bookstore with premises situated at No. 88
Burkill Road has for more than a year acted as the general dis-
tribution agent for the "Social News" (社会新闻), a bi-weekly
mosquito paper which devotes its pages to the exposing of react-
ionary elements and to advocating national unity. It is def-
initely of an anti-communist nature and attempts to show its
readers the fallacies and drawbacks of the "red" doctrine.
Although only a mosquito paper it enjoys a fairly large circu-
lation and is well received locally. The paper has its
editorial and printing offices at the Social News Agency at
premises located next to the headquarters of the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, West Gate, Nantao, its editor
being one Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村), a reformed communist.
Although it has not been definitely ascertained, it is believed
that this publication receives some sort of financial support
from the local Kuomintang authorities so that the latter's
views on the failings of radicalism can be broadcast.

student type entered the front door of the Hsin Kwang Bookstore
and stated that they wished to subscribe to the Social News.
One of these individuals gave his name as Wong Ts Dee (王志田)
and declared that he was a student at the Great China University,
off Kiaochow Road, O.O.L. Almost immediately afterwards
four similar youths entered the shop, one asking to be allowed

Date November 12, 1933.

Subject (in full) Smashing of shop window of the Liang Yue bookshop situated at No.851 North Szechuen Road.

Made by D.S.Glanville, Forwarded by Det.Inspr. A.Telfer.

Sir,
At about 12.15 p.m. 12/11/33, an assistant in a exchange shop situated at No.847 North Szechuen Road, heard the sound of glass being broken in the adjoining shop, No.851, the Liang Yue bookshop, so he went out and found that some unknown person had smashed the plate glass window of these premises. He did not see anyone running away from the scene. The sound of breaking glass was also heard by an assistant of the bookshop, one Lee Ching Kwong (李權慶), who at the time was in a back room having his tiffin, he also rushed out, but could see no one. In the doorway of the shop was found a quantity of small pamphlets, with a slogan printed in Chinese on them (attached). The translation is as follows:-
"Union of the people for the suppression of Communists."
The shop assistant reported the matter to C.P.C.1371, who reported the matter to the station. Enquiries were made by the undersigned and C.D.C.116, when the following was learned. The Liang Yue bookshop is closed on Sunday, and there is only one shop assistant left in charge of the premises, the master Woo Liang Dah (伍聯德), and the other assistants, living out. The assistant does not know where his master lives, except that he thinks it is on Yuen Yuen Road. He does not know whether his master is interested in any political party, but stated that there were some Russian books, translated into Chinese; on sale at the shop.
D.S.Moore of the Political Branch was informed of the occurrence.
The master of the shop will be interviewed on the morning of the 13/11/33.
Enquiries proceeding.

China Times and other local newspapers:
（批：November 14 1933）
LIANG YOU PUBLISHING COMPANY (良友) ATTACKED

Following the attack made by a crowd of rowdies dressed like workmen on the Nee Hwa Motion Picture Company's new studio (藝華公司) at Connaught Road at 9 a.m. on Sunday and the distribution of leaflets bearing the name of the Chinese Motion Picture Employees Federation for the Extermination of Communists, a second attack was made yesterday at 11 p.m. on the Liang You Publishing Co. at 851 North Szechuen Road.
At the hour mentioned, a man carrying an iron bar in his hands appeared in front of the premises and smashed a large window, afterwards making good his escape.
Upon receipt of a report regarding the attack police from Hongkew Station rushed to the scene and made an investigation.
It is generally thought that the attack on the Nee Hwa Motion Picture Co. is related to the attempt made on the Liang You Publishing Co. inasmuch as both places are suspected of propagating communism.
When the incident which occurred at the Liang You Publishing Co. became known, the Kwang Hwa Book Store at Foochow Road became alarmed and made an appeal to the Central Police Station for protection.
Yesterday the Liang You Publishing Co. sent the following letter, but we are not certain whether the letter was despatched before or after the attack was made.
"Yesterday the news that the Nee Hwa Co. was wrecked appeared in the columns of your paper, and the name of our company was mentioned.
